subject: javascript
summary: Covers DOM element selection and manipulation, event propagation phases (capturing, target, bubbling), and the event delegation pattern for handling dynamic elements efficiently.
key_points: Events propagate in three phases: capturing (top-down), target, and bubbling (bottom-up).
Event delegation attaches a single listener to a parent to handle events on dynamic child elements.
Use textContent instead of innerHTML for user input to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.
misconceptions: e.target and e.currentTarget always refer to the same element.
querySelectorAll returns a standard JavaScript array.
Event listeners on existing elements automatically apply to dynamically added children.
check_questions: What are the three phases of event propagation in the DOM?
Why is event delegation preferred over attaching listeners to individual dynamic elements?
What is the security risk of using innerHTML with user-provided content?

fact_candidates: Event propagation has three phases: capturing, target, and bubbling.
querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList; getElementsByTagName returns a live HTMLCollection.
practical_judgment_candidates: Choosing textContent over innerHTML when rendering user input.
Deciding whether to use event delegation or direct listeners based on dynamic content.
error_interpretation_candidates: XSS vulnerability from injecting unsanitized HTML via innerHTML.
Event listener not firing on dynamically added elements due to missing delegation.
scenario_candidates: Predicting the order of console.log outputs in a bubbling/capturing example.
Reading an event delegation handler to determine which clicks are processed.
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Confusing e.target (actual clicked element) with e.currentTarget (listener element).
Assuming querySelectorAll results support array methods like map directly.
